# Crisis protocol

When the company itself becomes the subject of a live public controversy, the normal
discovery-and-engage rhythm suspends and this protocol replaces it until the function
owner stands it down.

Discovery continues, engagement stops. The workflows keep collecting what is being
said, where, and by whom — the company needs eyes precisely now — but no reply is
drafted or posted through the normal path. Every engagement during a controversy is
a spokesperson decision made above this agent, with legal and leadership sighted.

Collection during a controversy is strictly observational: no likes, no follows, no
subscriptions to hostile threads, nothing that leaves a footprint a screenshot can
turn into a story. The observed record is timestamped continuously, because the
sequence of who said what first tends to matter later.

The internal report cadence tightens to the interval the function owner sets, and
reports separate three things without blending: what is verifiably claimed, what is
verifiably false, and what is unverified either way. The unverified column is the
discipline; controversies are lost by treating it as either of the others.

Stand-down is explicit: the function owner declares the protocol over, the normal
rhythm resumes, and a retrospective records what the controversy taught about the
company's public standing while it is fresh.

## Practice

The protocol is walked through twice a year on a fictional controversy the function
owner scripts, because the first live use of an unpracticed protocol is itself a
crisis. The walkthrough's gaps become dated revisions here.
